report.interpretation: Average claim cost is incurred (paid plus open reserve) divided by claim count, by loss date. I used auto claims whose repair shop is in the Chicago metro (RS-037, RS-039, RS-041), all causes. I compared Mar–Sep 2026 with Jan 2025–Feb 2026. Claims are counted at their current status as of the 2026-09-30 extract.
report.answer: The increase is real. Average cost at Chicago shops rose from about $3,482 (153 claims, Jan 2025–Feb 2026) to about $5,472 (61 claims, Mar–Sep 2026). Two things drive it, and both involve the non-preferred shop RS-041 Campbell Body Works. (1) Mix shift: RS-041's share of Chicago shop claims rose from about 26% to about 66%. The two preferred shops' average cost stayed flat or slightly lower, at $3,066 before and $2,900 after. (2) Higher cost at RS-041: its average rose from $4,699 to $6,822, and its collision claims rose from about $5,882 to $8,160. Nothing in the data points to weather, because the weather table has no events for Chicago or Illinois. The reloaded March payments do not explain it. The data isn't clear on why claims moved to RS-041. Samples are small (4–13 claims a month), so monthly figures are noisy, and Sept 2026 is incomplete.
report.answer_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) paid from claim_payments group by 1) select case when c.loss_date>='2026-03-01' then 'Mar-Sep 2026' else 'Jan 2025-Feb 2026' end period, count(*) claims, round(avg(c.reserve_amount+coalesce(p.paid,0))) avg_cost, round(avg((s.network_status='non-preferred')::int)*100,1) nonpref_share_pct, round(avg(case when s.network_status='preferred' then c.reserve_amount+coalesce(p.paid,0) end)) avg_preferred, round(avg(case when s.network_status='non-preferred' then c.reserve_amount+coalesce(p.paid,0) end)) avg_nonpreferred from claims c join repair_shops s using(repair_shop_id) left join p using(claim_id) where s.metro='Chicago' and c.product='auto' group by 1 order by 1 desc

findings.claim: Chicago shop average cost rose about 57%, driven by a shift of claims to non-preferred shop RS-041 and by higher costs at that shop. Preferred shops were flat.
findings.evidence_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) paid from claim_payments group by 1) select case when c.loss_date>='2026-03-01' then 'post' else 'pre' end per, s.repair_shop_id, s.network_status, c.cause, count(*) n, round(avg(c.reserve_amount+coalesce(p.paid,0))) avg_inc from claims c join repair_shops s using(repair_shop_id) left join p using(claim_id) where s.metro='Chicago' and c.product='auto' and c.loss_date<'2026-09-01' group by all order by 2,3,1,4

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mix shift toward the non-preferred shop RS-041
hypotheses.evidence: RS-041's share of Chicago shop claims rose from about 26% to about 66%. Monthly non-preferred share was 50–80% from Feb 2026, against about 0–38% in 2025.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher cost per claim at RS-041, the non-preferred shop
hypotheses.evidence: RS-041 collision average rose from $5,882 to $8,160 and its overall average from $4,699 to $6,822. Preferred shops did not rise.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data problem: duplicate payments loaded in the reload-2026-03-14 batch
hypotheses.evidence: The 159 duplicate rows cover payments from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13. Only a few Chicago claims in Jan–Feb 2026 are touched, and removing them does not change Mar–Sep averages.
weather_events has no rows for Chicago or Illinois. Hail claims in Chicago are few.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Incomplete recent months or open reserves
hypotheses.evidence: Sept 2026 is still filling in and has only 4 claims. Excluding it does not change the pattern, but open reserves can still move the averages.
Monthly counts are small (1–13 per shop). The mix shift is persistent across 7 months, which is more than noise, but individual high-cost months such as Aug 2026 at $8,655 are volatile.

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 duplicated payment rows in load batch reload-2026-03-14 (payments 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13)
data_quality_issues.impact: Slightly overstates paid and incurred for a few claims. Checked, and it has no effect on the Chicago increase.

data_quality_issues.issue: Recent loss months are incomplete because claims are reported late (Sept 2026 about 79% reported). A few outlier reserves exist (max $178k).
data_quality_issues.impact: Sept 2026 Chicago figures rest on very few claims and are unreliable.

proposed_actions.title: Review RS-041 Campbell Body Works (Chicago, non-preferred) repair costs and claim steering
proposed_actions.reason: Its share of Chicago claims has about tripled and its collision claims cost about 39% more than before. Check whether customers are being steered there, and whether estimates are being reviewed.

open_questions: Why are more Chicago customers using RS-041 since early 2026? Possible causes are agent or channel referrals, closure or capacity limits at the preferred shops, or a change in policy mix.
